title: Use the calculator for $\bar x$, $\sigma$, $\sum x$, $\sum x^2$
body: Enter data (with frequency column on). Read $\bar x$, $\sigma_x$ (population, the one S1 uses), $\sum x$, $\sum x^2$. Switch to 2-VAR for $S_{xy}$ values and the regression line directly.

title: Variance and standard deviation
body: $\sigma^2=\dfrac{\sum x^2}n-\bar x^2$ (the "mean of squares minus square of mean"). With frequencies, $\sum fx^2/\sum f-\bar x^2$. $S_{xx}=\sum x^2-\dfrac{(\sum x)^2}n=n\sigma^2$.

title: Coding
body: If $y=\dfrac{x-a}b$ then $\bar x=a+b\bar y$ and $\sigma_x=|b|\,\sigma_y$. Adding a constant changes the mean but **not** the standard deviation; multiplying scales both.

title: Combining two groups
body: Combined mean $=\dfrac{n_1\bar x_1+n_2\bar x_2}{n_1+n_2}$. For combined variance get each group's $\sum x^2=n(\sigma^2+\bar x^2)$, add them, divide by total $n$ and subtract the new mean squared.

title: Missing observation
body: Use the sum: new $\sum x=n\bar x-\text{removed}+\text{added}$; same for $\sum x^2$. Never re-enter the whole data set.

title: Grouped data
body: Use class midpoints in the calculator with frequencies. Means and variances are **estimates**. **Median by interpolation:** $Q=L+\dfrac{\text{position}-\text{cumulative frequency before}}{f}\times\text{width}$ with position $=\dfrac n2$ (median), $\dfrac n4$ ($Q_1$), $\dfrac{3n}4$ ($Q_3$). Use the class boundaries (not the labels) for $L$ and width.

title: Histograms
body: Frequency density $=\dfrac{\text{frequency}}{\text{class width}}$ and **area $\propto$ frequency**. So when one bar is known (area $=$ frequency), every other frequency is area$\times$(that scale). Bar heights from a given frequency: divide by the width.

title: Outliers
body: $x<Q_1-1.5\,\mathrm{IQR}$ or $x>Q_3+1.5\,\mathrm{IQR}$. Alternative given rule: beyond $\bar x\pm k\sigma$ ($k$ stated). Say which rule you used, and **show the numerical limits**.

title: Skewness from quartiles
body: $(Q_3-Q_2)-(Q_2-Q_1)>0$ positive skew, $<0$ negative; $0$ roughly symmetric. Mean $>$ median for positive skew. Quote the numbers.

title: Box plot
body: Five values: min, $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $Q_3$, max, with outliers marked separately (whiskers stop at the last non-outlier). To compare two distributions say something about **a measure of location and a measure of spread**, in context.

title: Stem-and-leaf
body: Always give a key ($2\,|\,3$ means $2.3$). The shape also gives the median by counting.

title: Percentiles and deciles
body: position $\dfrac{k}{100}n$; interpolate if grouped.

title: Interquartile range vs standard deviation
body: IQR resists outliers; $\sigma$ uses every value. Choose accordingly in "which measure is better" questions.

title: Mean from a frequency table with a missing value
body: set up $\bar x=\dfrac{\sum fx}{\sum f}$ with the unknown $f$ and solve the linear equation.

title: Range, mode, median checks
body: The median lies between the quartiles; the mean lies between min and max; $\sigma\le\dfrac{\text{range}}2$ (population SD $\le$ half the range).

title: Calculator 2-VAR does everything
body: Gives $a$, $b$ and $r$ directly. Still show the working lines your paper requires.

title: Formulae with $S$ notation
body:
$$S_{xx}=\sum x^2-\frac{(\sum x)^2}n,\quad S_{yy}=\sum y^2-\frac{(\sum y)^2}n,\quad S_{xy}=\sum xy-\frac{\sum x\sum y}n,$$
$$b=\frac{S_{xy}}{S_{xx}},\qquad a=\bar y-b\bar x,\qquad r=\frac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx}S_{yy}}}.$$

title: The line passes through $(\bar x,\bar y)$
body: So given the equation and $\bar x$, you get $\bar y$ (or the reverse) with no data. Two-point lines (e.g., the quartile points) can be found by the same logic.

title: Coding and $r$
body: Adding constants or multiplying **both** variables by positive constants **does not change $r$**. Multiplying exactly one variable by a negative constant changes the **sign** of $r$. Regression gradient scales: if $y'=cy$, $x'=dx$ then $b'=\dfrac cd\,b$.

title: Interpreting $b$ and $a$
body: "For each extra unit of $x$, $y$ increases by $b$ on average." The intercept $a$ is the predicted $y$ at $x=0$ — **only meaningful if $x=0$ is in context**.

title: Interpolation vs extrapolation
body: Predictions inside the data range are reliable (interpolation); outside are not. Always comment.

title: Correlation is not causation
body: a third factor may drive both. Quote context.

title: Which variable is $x$?
body: The **explanatory** (controlled/independent) variable is $x$. Regression of $y$ on $x$ minimises vertical distances; do not rearrange it to predict $x$ from $y$.

title: $r$ close to $\pm1$
body: strong linear; near $0$: **no linear** correlation (there may still be a curve). A scatter diagram helps.

title: Hypothesis-type comparison with critical value
body: (if given tables): $|r|>$ critical value means significant.

title: Residuals
body: residual $=y-\hat y$; positive means the point is above the line. Sum of residuals is $0$.

title: Spearman rank (beyond spec)
body: $r_s=1-\dfrac{6\sum d^2}{n(n^2-1)}$ for ranks without ties.

title: $r^2$ (beyond spec)
body: the proportion of the variation in $y$ explained by the line.

title: Fill a Venn diagram from the intersection outward
body: Start with $A\cap B$, then $A$-only $=P(A)-P(A\cap B)$, $B$-only likewise, and outside $=1-P(A\cup B)$. Every probability in the question becomes a number in a region.

title: Core formulae
body: $$P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B),\quad P(A\mid B)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)},\quad P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B\mid A).$$

title: Independent
body: $\Leftrightarrow P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)\Leftrightarrow P(A\mid B)=P(A)$. **Mutually exclusive** $\Leftrightarrow P(A\cap B)=0$. **A common error: mutually exclusive events with nonzero probabilities are never independent.**

title: "At least one" $=1-$ "none"
body: $P(\ge1)=1-P(\text{none})$; for independent attempts $1-(1-p)^n$.

title: Tree diagrams
body: **Multiply along branches, add across routes.** Without replacement, change the denominators on the second set of branches.

title: De Morgan
body: $P(A'\cap B')=1-P(A\cup B)$; $P(A'\cup B')=1-P(A\cap B)$; $P(A\cap B')=P(A)-P(A\cap B)$.

title: Exactly one of $A,B$
body: $P(A)+P(B)-2P(A\cap B)$.

title: Conditional probability by restricting the sample space
body: "given $B$" means zoom into $B$'s region of the Venn diagram or tree and divide by its total.

title: Bayes in one line
body: $P(A\mid B)=\dfrac{P(A)P(B\mid A)}{P(B)}$ with $P(B)$ from the tree (add the routes that give $B$).

title: Sample-space grid for two dice or two spinners
body: Count favourable cells over $36$; sums: $7$ has $6$ ways, $2$ and $12$ one way.

title: Combinations for "choose without replacement"
body: (beyond spec in places): drawing $k$ of colour 1 from $a$ and $n-k$ of colour 2 from $b$: $\dfrac{\binom ak\binom b{n-k}}{\binom{a+b}n}$. Faster than a long tree.

title: Probabilities that sum to 1
body: use this to find an unknown $x$ in a table of probabilities; **each must be between 0 and 1**, so reject roots outside.

title: Finding unknowns from two conditions
body: e.g. independence gives a product equation, and the union gives a sum equation; solve the pair (quadratic).

title: Geometric-type "first success on trial $n$"
body: (beyond spec): $q^{n-1}p$.

title: Expected number of successes (beyond spec)
body: $np$.

title: Binomial (beyond spec)
body: $P(X=r)=\binom nrp^rq^{n-r}$; calculator "BinomialPD/CD".

title: Probability always in $[0,1]$, so check every result
Distribution table checks
body: $\sum p=1$; **use this to find $k$** first.

title: $E(X)=\sum xp$; $E(X^2)=\sum x^2p$; $\mathrm{Var}(X)=E(X^2)-[E(X)]^2$
body: The variance is **never negative**: if it is, you subtracted the wrong way.

title: Transformations
body: $E(aX+b)=aE(X)+b$; $\mathrm{Var}(aX+b)=a^2\mathrm{Var}(X)$; sd scales by $|a|$. The **$+b$ drops out of the variance**.

title: $E[g(X)]=\sum g(x)p(x)$
body: apply the function to each value, not to $E(X)$. **$E(X^2)\ne[E(X)]^2$.**

title: Sums of variables
body: $E(X+Y)=E(X)+E(Y)$ always; $\mathrm{Var}(X\pm Y)=\mathrm{Var}(X)+\mathrm{Var}(Y)$ **only for independent**. Both **plus**, even for $X-Y$.

title: Unknown $a,b$ in a table
body: set up simultaneous equations from $\sum p=1$ and the given $E(X)$ (or a given probability).

title: Cumulative distribution $F(x)=P(X\le x)$
body: $P(X=x)=F(x)-F(x^-)$ (difference with the previous value). $P(X>x)=1-F(x)$.

title: Symmetric distribution
body: mean is the centre, so no need to calculate $E(X)$ at all. Variance uses the squared distance from the centre.

title: Discrete uniform on $1,\dots,n$
body: $E(X)=\dfrac{n+1}2$, $\mathrm{Var}(X)=\dfrac{n^2-1}{12}$. For a fair die $E=3.5$, $\mathrm{Var}=\dfrac{35}{12}$.

title: A fair game
body: expected gain $=0$. Expected profit per play $=E(\text{winnings})-\text{stake}$.

title: Mode vs mean vs median
body: mode has the greatest probability; median is where cumulative probability crosses $0.5$.

title: Standard deviation of $aX+b$
body: $|a|\sigma$. Check units.

title: Linear function trick
body: if $Y=aX+b$ and you know $E(Y)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(Y)$, invert to get $E(X)=\dfrac{E(Y)-b}a$, $\mathrm{Var}(X)=\dfrac{\mathrm{Var}(Y)}{a^2}$.

title: Expectation of a count
body: if each trial succeeds with probability $p$ the expected number is $np$ (beyond spec).

title: Standardise
body: $Z=\dfrac{X-\mu}\sigma\sim N(0,1)$. **Sketch the bell, shade the area**, then read the table or use calculator "Normal CD".

title: Two unknowns $\mu,\sigma$
body: Standardise both conditions to get two **linear** equations: $\dfrac{x_1-\mu}\sigma=z_1$, $\dfrac{x_2-\mu}\sigma=z_2$. Subtract: $\sigma=\dfrac{x_2-x_1}{z_2-z_1}$, then back-substitute for $\mu$. Mind the **signs of $z$**.

title: Quartiles of a normal
body: $Q_1=\mu-0.6745\sigma$, $Q_3=\mu+0.6745\sigma$, so $\mathrm{IQR}=1.349\sigma$. Handy when a question gives quartiles and asks for $\sigma$.

title: 68–95–99.7 rule
body: about $68\%$ within $\mu\pm\sigma$, $95\%$ within $\pm2\sigma$, $99.7\%$ within $\pm3\sigma$ — for sanity checks and quick estimates.

title: Given $P(X>a)$ and $P(X<b)$ to find $\mu$ only
body: use the single standardised equation.

title: "Same mean, different standard deviation"
body: sketch both curves; the larger-$\sigma$ curve is wider and lower. A smaller $\sigma$ puts more probability near the mean.

title: Normal approximation to binomial (beyond spec)
body: $X\sim B(n,p)\approx N(np,\,npq)$ when $np>5$ and $nq>5$; **continuity correction**: $P(X\le k)\to P(Y<k+0.5)$, $P(X\ge k)\to P(Y>k-0.5)$.

title: Sums of independent normals (beyond spec)
body: $N(\mu_1,\sigma_1^2)\pm N(\mu_2,\sigma_2^2)$: means add or subtract, **variances always add**.

title: Probability of an exact value is $0$
body: $P(X=a)=0$, so $<$ and $\le$ are equivalent.

title: Working with proportions
body: a percentage of a population above $a$ is $P(X>a)\times100$. Number expected in a sample of $n$: $n\,P(\cdot)$.

title: Fitting a normal to data
body: take $\mu=\bar x$ and $\sigma=s$, then compare predicted vs observed.

title: Rounding
body: carry at least 4 significant figures of $z$ and only round the final answer.

title: Advantages and limitations of a model
body: Typical phrases: "simplifies a complex situation", "can make predictions", "may be refined"; limitations: "assumes independence", "assumes constant probability", "ignores outliers", "works only in the range of data".

title: Assumptions for a Normal model
body: continuous, symmetric, bell-shaped, unimodal. Check by comparing mean $\approx$ median, or skewness.

title: Independence assumption (and why it may fail)
body: State **in context**.

title: Show the rounding that proves a printed answer
source: Pearson WST01 Jan 2024 examiner report Q2(a)(ii)
body: In a "show that" question, display the formula, exact or unrounded substitution, and a value with more figures than the printed result. Check that the displayed value actually rounds to that result; merely copying the printed answer does not establish it.

title: Count a fraction of a grouped class
source: Pearson WST01 Jun 2022 examiner report Q3(c)
body: If a threshold $t$ lies within class $[L,U)$ of frequency $f$, estimate the number below it in that class as $f(t-L)/(U-L)$, assuming uniform spread within the class. Add the complete lower classes and check the partial count lies from $0$ to $f$.

title: Interpolate down from the upper boundary
source: Pearson WST01 Jun 2022 examiner report Q3(b)
body: If the desired rank $r$ is near the upper end of a class with upper boundary $U$, frequency $f$, width $w$, and cumulative frequency $C$ through the class, use $Q=U-(C-r)w/f$. Check it agrees with upward interpolation from the lower boundary.

title: Predict a change using only the gradient
source: Pearson WST01 Jun 2022 examiner report Q2(f)
body: For $\hat y=a+bx$ with $b\ne0$, a change $\Delta y$ corresponds to $\Delta x=\Delta y/b$; the intercept cancels. Check units and the sign of $b$ before interpreting the direction of change.

title: Find the regression slope from correlation and spread
source: derived
body: If $r,\sigma_x,\sigma_y$ are known and $\sigma_x>0$, the $y$-on-$x$ slope is $b=r\sigma_y/\sigma_x$. Check that its sign matches $r$ and its units are response units per explanatory unit.

title: Enter scaled predictor units literally
source: Pearson WST01 Jun 2022 examiner report Q2(e)
body: If a regression's $x$ is measured in millions, seven million means $x=7$ in the equation. Check the resulting prediction against the scale and range of the original data, and state the output units.

title: Keep the full gradient when finding the intercept
source: Pearson WST01 Jan 2024 examiner report Q4(b)
body: Compute $a=\bar y-b\bar x$ with the unrounded calculator value of $b$, then round the stated line as instructed. Check the displayed equation at $x=\bar x$; it should give approximately $\bar y$.

title: Check every denominator in sampling without replacement
source: Pearson WST01 Jun 2022 examiner report Q3(d)
body: For $k$ ordered draws from $N$ objects without replacement, denominators run $N(N-1)\cdots(N-k+1)$, and a repeated-success numerator also decreases. A denominator fixed at $N$ would model replacement, so inspect that pattern before multiplying.

title: Make stopping outcomes terminal immediately
source: Pearson WST01 Jun 2022 examiner report Q5(f)
body: In a game that ends on a specified result, draw no further branches after that result. Add the probabilities of all terminal leaves to check they total $1$.

title: Independence extends to complements
source: derived
body: If $A$ and $B$ are independent, then $P(A\cap B')=P(A)[1-P(B)]$. Cross-check by subtracting $P(A\cap B)$ from $P(A)$.

title: Keep three-set overlaps once
source: derived
body: For three events, use $P(A\cup B\cup C)=P(A)+P(B)+P(C)-P(A\cap B)-P(A\cap C)-P(B\cap C)+P(A\cap B\cap C)$. Check a mutually exclusive pair has zero pair and triple intersection before substituting.

title: Use a joint table for products unless independent
source: derived
body: For independent $X,Y$, $E(XY)=E(X)E(Y)$; otherwise compute $\sum_{x,y}xyP(X=x,Y=y)$ from the joint distribution. Check independence is stated or proved before multiplying separate means.

title: Merge equal products from two draws
source: Pearson WST01 Oct 2022 examiner report Q7(e,f)
body: With two independent draws with replacement, ordered pair $(x_i,x_j)$ has probability $p_ip_j$; combine pairs that yield the same product. Off-diagonal pairs contribute $2p_ip_j$ when both orders are possible, but a diagonal pair contributes $p_i^2$ only once.

title: Fix a discrete CDF at its upper endpoint
source: Pearson WST01 Jan 2024 examiner report Q7(a,b)
body: If the largest possible value is $m$, use $F(m)=1$ to find an unknown constant before differencing the CDF. Check that $F$ is nondecreasing and all successive differences are nonnegative.

title: Build a payoff table from terminal outcomes
source: derived
body: List each game's terminal route with its probability and net gain, including the entry fee exactly once, then calculate $E(G)=\sum g_ip_i$. Check route probabilities sum to $1$ before taking the expectation.

title: Solve a conditional normal quantile by CDF arithmetic
source: Pearson WST01 Jun 2022 examiner report Q6(c)
body: For $v<c$ and $P(X>v\mid X<c)=q$, write $[F(c)-F(v)]/F(c)=q$, then find $F(v)=(1-q)F(c)$ and invert once. Check $v<c$ and $0<F(v)<F(c)$.

title: Equal opposite tails locate the mean
source: derived
body: If $X$ is normal and $P(X<a)=P(X>b)$ with $a<b$, symmetry gives $\mu=(a+b)/2$ without a table. Check that $a$ and $b$ are equally far from this mean.

title: Simplify a cutoff containing the mean
source: Pearson WST01 Jan 2024 examiner report Q8
body: If a probability at cutoff $k\mu$ gives $(k\mu-\mu)/\sigma=z$, rewrite it at once as $(k-1)\mu=z\sigma$. Combine that short relation with the other condition and check $\sigma>0$.

title: Separate the normal model from the sampling model
source: Pearson WST01 Jan 2024 examiner report Q1(d)
body: First calculate $p=P(X>c)$; for two independent attempts, both exceeding $c$ has probability $p^2$. For two draws without replacement from a counted group with $M$ successes among $N$, use $M(M-1)/[N(N-1)]$ instead; check which model the question states.

title: Name both variables when interpreting correlation
source: Pearson WST01 Jun 2022 examiner report Q2(b)
body: State how the named response tends to change as the named explanatory variable increases, including strength and direction. Check that the sentence describes a relationship in context rather than merely saying "positive correlation".
